text:
Marathon Petroleum recovered 2.5% today after a three-day slide that had knocked the stock down 3.4% from its October 20th peak. The bounce came as oil prices fell on news that Saudi Arabia's defense minister is traveling to Iran for de-escalation talks—a sign that the immediate threat of wider Middle East conflict may be easing. That matters for refiners like Marathon because crude prices had spiked above $116 earlier this week on geopolitical fears, and lower oil costs improve refining margins (the profit spread between what crude costs and what refined products sell for).

The refining backdrop remains solid: U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity and oil storage levels are moderate, which keeps demand steady. Over the past week, the stock has essentially traded the oil price gyrations—up when crude spiked on Iran tensions, down when those tensions looked like they might boil over into attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Today's bounce reflects investor relief that cooler heads appear to be prevailing.
